title: Point only at what is on screen
statement: Never point anyone reading or marking an item at what they cannot see, like an off-screen label, code, highlight or line, or the brief and source facts behind it.
example: On about 28 word cards, the second hint told a student to reread a line they had not met and could not see.
detail: A review of the reading course found a question and its feedback citing a "Source C" that no passage, tag or heading in the lesson ever named, a label leaked from the source material, and internal span codes in a modelled think-aloud that nothing on the child's screen carried. The next review found that on about 28 word cards, which come before any passage and show no text, the second hint told the student to reread a line they had not met, and that nine hints sent students to reread a highlight that was never shown, because the highlighting data went only to the scorer.
